party-name-silver-lion: The Company of the Silver Lion
party-meeting-tavern: The company was born on a rainy night at the Drowned Goat, when {members} reached for the same last bowl of stew and decided, after a long silence, to share it.
party-meeting-caravan: One salt caravan to guard through the Ashen Pass, three ambushes and a sandstorm: by the end of the road, {members} had become a company.
party-meeting-prison: The company first met at the bottom of a cell beneath the duke's keep, for {count} different crimes; the escape that followed is still told in the taverns of the lower town.
party-meeting-notice: A single notice nailed to a temple door — “Brave souls wanted, no questions asked” — brought {members} to the same table, and the company has kept that table ever since.
party-meeting-shipwreck: The company was founded on a beach of black sand, the morning after the Gull's Promise sank. {members}: that is all the sea gave back, and no one has ever learned why.
party-meeting-duel: It began with a duel nobody won: when the guards arrived, {members} stood on the same side of the barricade, and the company was born before anyone had agreed to it.
party-meeting-fair: At the great fair of Valmor, a runaway drake set the market ablaze; {members} still stood between the fire and the children, and the town has toasted the company ever since.
party-meeting-letters: An old dying wizard wrote {count} letters to {count} strangers: they led {members} down the same road, and the company was formed at its end, before a sealed tomb.
party-meeting-guild: On the same day, the Adventurers' Guild turned away {members}; the company was formed the very next morning, out of pure stubbornness.
party-meeting-haunted-inn: A haunted inn, a stormy night and a ghost that only {count} people could see: by dawn, {members} had laid the ghost to rest, and the company was born.
party-meeting-war: The company comes from the last war: {members} served in the same doomed regiment, and when the order to retreat never came, the whole troop left of its own accord.
party-meeting-torn-map: The map was torn into {count} pieces, each with a different bearer: it took {members} a year of suspicion to admit that the pieces only made sense together, and the company was born that day.
party-goal-crown: Today the company seeks the Lost Crown of Aldermere, and the reward has already been sworn into {count} equal shares — even if nobody agrees on what “equal” means.
party-goal-grey-peaks: The company has taken the contract nobody else would: to find out what wakes beneath the Grey Peaks before it wakes completely.
party-goal-lich-debt: The company owes a great deal of gold to a very patient lich, and {first} swears that the next job will settle everything.
party-goal-relic: Bound by an oath sworn in a burning temple, the company searches for the relic that was saved from the flames and stolen the same night.
party-goal-moon-map: The company follows a map that changes every full moon, convinced that one day it will finally stop on the right place.
party-goal-tourney: The company has entered the Grand Tourney of Valmor under a false banner: {first} handles the lies, the rest of the troop handles the winning.
party-goal-silent-child: The company escorts a silent child across the kingdom, and every inn along the road seems to know more about the child than the troop itself.
party-goal-rift: The company hunts the cult that opened a rift above the capital, before the rift opens a little wider.
party-goal-song: The company wants one thing above all: a song. A real one, sung in every tavern, with all {count} names in it.
party-goal-blood-list: The company keeps a list of names written in blood on the back of a wanted poster, and crosses them out one by one.
party-goal-ruined-keep: The company has bought a ruined keep with its last coins, and dreams of turning it into a fortress before winter — or at least before the roof falls in.
party-goal-fallen-star: A star fell north of the Mistwood, and the company means to reach it first, ahead of three kingdoms and one very determined wizard.
